title: Exception handling middleware (UseExceptionHandler)
hook: Unhandled exceptions in your Web API should become consistent JSON Problem Details responses — not raw stack traces. The exception handling middleware must wrap the entire pipeline as the outermost onion layer.

blocks.text: Exception handling middleware catches exceptions thrown anywhere inside the pipeline after routing, authentication, or your controller. In development, UseDeveloperExceptionPage shows detailed errors. In production, UseExceptionHandler redirects to an error path or invokes a custom handler that returns RFC 7807 Problem Details — a standard JSON shape with type, title, status, and detail fields.

entries.plainDefinition: Middleware that catches unhandled exceptions and runs a separate error pipeline.

entries.longForm: RFC 7807 Problem Details for HTTP APIs
entries.plainDefinition: Standard JSON error format with type, title, status, detail, and optional extensions.
.NET 8+ service-based handler registered in DI; TryHandleAsync returns true if handled.
Development-only middleware showing exception page with stack trace.

blocks.text: Clients and API gateways expect predictable error JSON. Leaking stack traces violates security baselines. Without outer exception middleware, Kestrel may abort the connection or return HTML. Correlation IDs in Problem Details extensions help trace one failed request across logs and Application Insights. Senior interviews ask how exception handling interacts with middleware order and whether filters replace middleware.

blocks.title: Middleware vs exception filter
blocks.body: Exception filters run inside MVC pipeline only. Middleware catches exceptions from minimal APIs, middleware, and anything outside controller filters. Use both: middleware for global fallback, filters for controller-specific mapping.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Inner middleware or endpoint throws
items.body: Exception bubbles up the async call stack through await _next frames.

items.title: Outer exception handler catches
items.body: UseExceptionHandler intercepts before Kestrel sees an unhandled fault.

items.title: Error pipeline runs
items.body: Re-executes pipeline toward /error or invokes IExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync.

items.title: Problem Details written
items.body: Response status set, body serialized, connection completed cleanly.

diagram.title: Exception unwind to outer handler
diagram.source:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Client
  participant EH as Exception Handler
  participant Auth
  participant EP as Endpoint
  Client->>EH: HTTP request
  EH->>Auth: await next
  Auth->>EP: await next
  EP-->>Auth: throws Exception
  Auth-->>EH: propagates
  EH->>EH: handle + Problem Details
  EH->>Client: 500 application/problem+json

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Swallowing exceptions in custom middleware without rethrow — downstream never sees failure but state may be corrupt. Registering UseExceptionHandler after MapControllers. Returning exception.Message to clients in production. Forgetting AddProblemDetails when using IProblemDetailsService.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: Application Insights tracks exceptions with operation_Id matching TraceIdentifier. Alert on spike in 500 without application/problem+json content type — indicates handler bypass. Use dotnet-counters for exception rate. For double-fault scenarios (handler itself throws), ASP.NET Core falls back to server abort — keep handlers minimal and test them. Polly resilience exceptions may be handled inside HttpClient pipeline, not your API exception middleware — distinguish outbound from inbound.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: Misses minimal API throws unless duplicated
Clients must parse extensions for domain codes

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying exception filters alone are enough for a mixed minimal API + controller app. Not knowing exception handler must be first middleware. Unable to describe Problem Details or why stack traces in production are unacceptable. Claiming try/catch in every action is the correct global strategy.

interviewTakeaways: UseExceptionHandler is outermost middleware — it catches exceptions unwinding from inner layers.
Problem Details (RFC 7807) is the standard API error body; add correlationId in extensions.
Production tip: integration-test /throw endpoint for application/problem+json; alert if 500 returns HTML.

60s: Exception handler wraps the onion. Throws propagate outward to it. IExceptionHandler maps to Problem Details. Filters only cover MVC inside controllers. Register handler before routing. Developer page dev-only.
Follow-up: what happens if the exception handler itself throws?
commonPitfalls: Saying 'I use [HandleError] on every action' gets you rejected — not DRY and misses minimal APIs.
UseExceptionHandler after MapControllers — unhandled controller exceptions escape.

Strong answer: 'Outermost UseExceptionHandler. IExceptionHandler + Problem Details. correlationId in extensions. WebApplicationFactory proves JSON errors. Filters for controller-specific mapping only.'
introducedIn: ASP.NET Core 1.0; IExceptionHandler and IProblemDetailsService in .NET 7/8

jsTsCorrelations.note: Express (err, req, res, next) runs when next(err) is called or async errors reach the framework. ASP.NET exception handler catches unhandled throws similarly but sits at the outer pipeline shell.

NestJS @Catch() filters map exceptions to HTTP responses like IExceptionHandler, but Nest applies them at framework layer after guards. ASP.NET splits middleware (global) vs MVC filters (controller scope).
